claims.supporting_quote: In a landmark 14-year Purina study published in 2002, Labrador retrievers fed 25 percent fewer calories than their littermates, stayed leaner, developed chronic disease later, and lived a median of nearly two years longer.

claims.claim: A mouse study linked STING signals from marrow fat cells to inflammation and declining NAD+ in bone-forming cells, and interrupting the pathway helped preserve aging bone.
claims.episode_span: A mouse study links STING-mediated signals from marrow fat cells to inflammation and to declining NAD+ in bone-forming cells, and interrupting that pathway helped preserve aging bone.
claims.source_title: Blocking STING Helps Preserve Bone in Aging Mice
claims.supporting_quote: A new study links STING-mediated signals from marrow fat cells to inflammation and declining NAD⁺ levels in bone-forming cells. Interrupting this pathway helped preserve aging bone

claims.claim: A 2014 commentary said Deelen et al. in Human Molecular Genetics reported the largest genome-wide association study of human longevity to that date, and that rodent lifespan genes were not consistently associated with human longevity.
claims.episode_span: Deelen and colleagues published in Human Molecular Genetics a genome-wide association study of human longevity.
claims.source_title: Why genes extending lifespan in model organisms have not been consistently associated with human longevity and what it means to translation research
claims.supporting_quote: A recent paper by Deelen et al. (2014) in Human Molecular Genetics reports the largest genome-wide association study of human longevity to date. While impressive, there is a remarkable lack of association of genes known to considerably extend lifespan in rodents with human longevity, both in this latest study and in genetic association studies in general.

claims.claim: The 2014 commentary hypothesized that limited genetic diversity in model-organism strains, and strain-specific caloric-restriction effects, limit translation of aging genetics to human therapies.
claims.episode_span: Most of those studies use strains of limited genetic diversity.
claims.source_title: Why genes extending lifespan in model organisms have not been consistently associated with human longevity and what it means to translation research
claims.supporting_quote: In particular, most studies in model organisms are conducted in strains of limited genetic diversity which are then not applicable to human populations.

claims.claim: In Snell dwarf mouse livers, Akt/PKB and p38 MAPK phosphorylation and kinase activity, and phosphorylation of downstream translation regulators, were decreased.
claims.episode_span: found lower phosphorylation and lower kinase activity of Akt, also called PKB, and of p38 MAPK, and lower phosphorylation of downstream regulators of translation.
claims.source_title: Akt/PKB and p38 MAPK signaling, translational initiation and longevity in Snell dwarf mouse livers
claims.supporting_quote: Our data indicate that the phosphorylation and kinase activities of Akt/PKB and p38 MAPK, and the levels of phosphorylation of downstream regulators of translation are decreased in dwarf mouse livers.

claims.claim: Longevity of the Snell dwarf Pit-1 mouse has been associated with reduced insulin/IGF-1/GH signaling, and the 2004 authors propose that down-regulation of protein synthesis may characterize that mutation.
claims.episode_span: The Snell dwarf mouse carries a Pit-1 mutation. Its longevity has been associated with reduced insulin, IGF-1, and growth-hormone signaling.
claims.source_title: Akt/PKB and p38 MAPK signaling, translational initiation and longevity in Snell dwarf mouse livers
claims.supporting_quote: Studies have indicated that longevity of the Snell dwarf (Pit-1) mouse mutant is associated with the reduction of function of the insulin/IGF-1/GH signaling pathway.
